A. W. Greely, "Three Years of Arctic Service: An Account of the Lady Franklin Bay Expedition of 1881-84", vol. 1
(New York: Charles Scribner's Sons, 1886). Domínio público.
Texto completo (OCR): https://archive.org/details/threeyearsofarct01gree
Trechos transcritos do OCR com hifenização desfeita e erros óbvios de OCR corrigidos; "[...]" marca omissão.

[E1] (p. 40, July 1881) On July 4th, with all on board, the Proteus dropped to anchor off Queen's wharf, awaiting the final supplies. They came on the 7th, and at noon of that day we passed the majestic cliffs which form the narrows of St. John's, and turned our prow toward Greenland with fine weather, blue sky, and favoring wind.

[E2] (pp. 78-79, Aug. 1881) On the morning of the 11th the sky showed signs of clearing, and at 7 a.m., under the influence of a southwesterly gale, the fog lifted to the northward. [...] On reaching the entrance of Discovery Harbor, a narrow channel free from ice was found [...]. The Proteus steamed slowly into the curved water-space to the northward of Dutch Island, the powerful engines stopped, an ice-anchor was thrown on the harbor-floe, and our voyage to Lady Franklin Bay was prosperously ended.

[E3] (p. 86, Aug. 1881) Lieutenant Lockwood, with the launch, attempted to follow the Proteus as she left her anchorage on the morning of the 19th, but owing to the extremely heavy ice found it impossible to do so.
